Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Valerie Cole, DOB: 19/09/1993, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon
- Referring GP: Dr. Smith, Practice: Babylon (teleconsultation), Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood, work-related (onset within ~2 months of starting a new, highly stressful job; prominent work-focused anxiety, insomnia, anhedonia)
- Secondary: Insomnia secondary to anxiety/occupational stress (sleep latency “hours,” total ~3–4 hours/night)
- Tertiary: Depressive symptoms (low mood, anhedonia, fatigue) without suicidality
(DDx consistent with transcript: consider Generalized Anxiety Disorder (early course) and Major Depressive Episode with anxious distress if symptoms persist/generalize.)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: None reported (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Not recorded

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: None reported
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): None reported
- Family History: Mother with history of depression

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with parents
- Social Support: Reports good family support
- Occupation/Education: New role at a fashion retailer head office; reports significant stress; supervisor described as “not very nice”; working late hours
- Alcohol Use: Binge drinking most weekends (exceeds limits by patient report); occasional glass of wine during the week; exact amounts not quantified
- Smoking/Substance Use: Occasional smoking; denies illicit drug use
- Key Stressors: New job demands, supervisor conflict, commute on crowded/airless tube, fear of being late, performance concerns

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not recorded
- Mood & Affect: Reports feeling very anxious and down; anhedonia; affect not recorded
- Speech & Thought: Speech not recorded; thought content notable for excessive worry about work and performance; denies suicidal ideation
- Perception: Not recorded

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded
- Attention/Concentration: Not recorded
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Acknowledges problem and seeks help; otherwise not recorded

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Difficulty initiating sleep (hours), early awakening with palpitations; estimated 3–4 hours/night; non-restorative
- Appetite: No significant change; increased chocolate intake
- Motivation/Energy: Markedly reduced energy; loss of interest in previously enjoyed activities (running, tennis, socializing)
- Anxiety Symptoms: Morning dread, anticipatory anxiety about work/being late, palpitations (perceived irregular/rapid, minutes to ~10 minutes), feeling “on edge,” avoidance of social activities and public transport (tube stressful)

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Denies suicidal ideation; no self-harm; risk to others not recorded
- Protective Factors: Supportive family; employed; help-seeking; willingness to engage in therapy
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low based on denial of suicidality and presence of supports
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
- Predisposing: Family history of depression (mother)
- Precipitating: Onset after starting a new, highly stressful job with supervisory conflict; stressful commute; fear of lateness
- Perpetuating: Sleep deprivation; ongoing workplace stress; avoidance of activities; weekend binge alcohol use potentially worsening sleep/anxiety; persistent worry
- Protective: Supportive parents; motivation to seek help; openness to therapy; no current suicidality
Overall presentation is most consistent with an adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood related to occupational stress, with significant insomnia and somatic anxiety (palpitations). Medical contributors to palpitations/anxiety (e.g., thyroid abnormalities, anemia) are planned to be screened via basic blood tests.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce daily anxiety; improve sleep; cope better with work-related stress; continue functioning at work
- Clinical Goal(s): Decrease anxiety and depressive symptoms; restore sleep continuity; improve functioning and engagement in previously enjoyed activities
- Actions (Patient):
  - Self-refer to NHS talking therapy (CBT-based) via link to be provided by GP
  - Begin recommended online resources provided by GP while awaiting therapy
  - Call GP if anxiety worsens or coping at work/with daily activities becomes difficult
  - Call support line to arrange basic blood tests; attend tests and subsequent review
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide self-referral link for NHS talking therapy
  - Provide online mental health and sleep resource information
  - Arrange basic blood tests (per plan) and schedule GP follow-up approximately one week after tests to review results
  - Consider pharmacotherapy if significant symptoms persist or worsen despite therapy and self-management (medication not first line per discussion)

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
Insomnia related to anxiety/occupational stress
- Patient Goal(s): Fall asleep more easily; achieve more restorative sleep
- Clinical Goal(s): Improve sleep latency and duration; reduce night-time anxiety/early morning awakenings
- Actions (Patient):
  - Implement sleep hygiene strategies provided by GP information
  - Use online resources suggested by GP to address anxiety and sleep
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide sleep hygiene guidance
  - Review sleep and anxiety symptoms at follow-up post–blood tests; consider stepped care if insomnia persists

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Nature of anxiety and stress response; talking therapy options and self-referral; online self-help resources; sleep hygiene; potential role of medication (not first line); plan for blood tests and follow-up; when to seek urgent review
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Inability to cope with work or daily routines; escalating anxiety/palpitations; further sleep reduction; increased avoidance
- Coping Strategies: Engage in online CBT-based tools; apply sleep hygiene strategies; seek support from family; contact GP if worsening

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes – agreed to therapy self-referral and blood tests
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None currently; self-referral to NHS talking therapy pending
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: Planned GP follow-up one week after completion of blood tests (exact date not recorded)

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Adjustment disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood (High): Onset within ~2 months of a clear work-related stressor with prominent anxiety, insomnia, and low mood
- Generalized anxiety disorder, early course (Medium): Excessive worry, sleep disturbance, fatigue; duration <6 months but symptom pattern consistent
- Major depressive episode with anxious distress (Medium): Low mood, anhedonia, insomnia, fatigue >2 weeks with significant anxious distress; anxiety appears primary with external trigger

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Gender, contact details, allergies, past medical history, full MSE (appearance, speech, cognition), emergency contact, exact review date not recorded
- Internal conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted
- Transcript quality notes: Minor incomplete/elliptical phrases typical of live teleconsultation; overall content understandable and sufficient for care planning
